Subject: RE: Sudden errors & latency spikes impacting checkout inference — initial triage

Vanessa / team — initial findings from the edge:

- Symptoms: rapid 5xx spike and p95 token latency increase aligning with ~07:42 PT. Affected requests show TCP retransmits and TLS handshake retries on a subset of egress peers to ShopLine's ASN.
- Traces: I pulled the first 100 failed request IDs Sophie sent and ran traceroutes from our egress fleet. See attached excerpt (shopline-traces.txt).
- Hypothesis: partial VPC-peering path degradation + intermittent NAT gateway overload in region us-west-2 causing serialization delays; DNS resolution appears inconsistent for a small fraction of requests (some resolve to stale / secondary endpoint).

Immediate actions taken:
1) Scoped affected hosts: ~18% of egress nodes saw >50% error amplification.
2) Redirected new requests away from those egress nodes to healthy pools (soft routing change) — this reduced errors by ~6% within 3m on our test cluster.
3) Disallowed a recent experimental route used for cheaper egress that was rolled out earlier this week (flagged in rollout metadata).

Next: we should either fully rollback that route or do a targeted traffic shift. If ShopLine is comfortable, recommend a rollback to the pre-deploy routing policy that was stable overnight.

Notes: full packet captures are already stored to the Drive link in the thread. I'm standing by on the incident channel.

— Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: shopline-traces.txt (trace excerpt)

Team — quick summary for execs and ShopLine:

- Root cause likely: combination of a partial peering route regression and a mis-sized NAT path that amplifies latency under burst. DNS inconsistencies increase error surface for pinned endpoints.
- Customer impact: ShopLine checkout failures (approx 10–18% error window) and p95 >2s for ~15 minutes at peak. Financial risk present; we need an exec sync within 60m.
- Recommended immediate mitigations:
  1) Full rollback of the experimental egress route (safe, quick).
  2) Increase NAT pool concurrency and shift traffic to alternate peering in another AZ.
  3) Ask ShopLine to temporarily remove client-side pinning to the failing endpoint (if possible).

I'll prepare a 2-slide exec brief and a short customer-facing note. Vanessa, want me to drop both in the incident channel and ping Marissa for approval before sending?

— Vivek

Subject: Incident update: routing regression identified and rollback in progress

Sophie — quick update and next steps: 

What we found: partial regression in an experimental egress routing policy (affecting a subset of egress peers) combined with transient NAT gateway saturation. DNS inconsistencies made some requests failover to affected peers.

What we're doing now:
- Executing a full rollback of the experimental route (started 08:30 PT).
- Increasing NAT pool concurrency and shifting traffic to an alternate peering via us-west-2 AZ-b.
- Monitoring ShopLine traffic in real time; filing a post-incident report once we have full logs.

Impact so far: initial rollback reduced error rate by ~11% on our staging replays; we expect production improvement within the next 5–12 minutes.

We will follow up with a short exec summary and a proposed permanent mitigation (disable that route on 2-week canary or add additional health checks).

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with highest priority.

— Vanessa
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
